execution_batches.description: Rebuild the workflow contract and graph so the new machine has one canonical context and one clean closure model.
Make success and failure persistence type-safe and uniform across every branch.
Update tests and manual validation assets while the rebuilt workflow is stabilizing.
Run local quality gates and direct AWS workflow validation against real DynamoDB-backed records.

tasks.title: Replace the current Step Functions definition with a clean minimal workflow graph
outputs: A new Express workflow definition that removes duplicated failure branches and uses the state set approved in the technical spec
exit_criteria: The workflow graph contains BootstrapWorkflowInput, AcquireIdempotencyLock, MarkPendingInProgress, RollbackIdempotencyLock, InvokeConsumerLambda, PrepareSuccessPersistence, PersistSuccessResult, MarkIdempotencyCompleted, MarkPendingCompleted, NormalizeTerminalFailure, NormalizeTransientExhaustedFailure, NormalizeTimeoutFailure, NormalizeUnexpectedFailure, PrepareFailurePersistence, PersistFailureResult, MarkIdempotencyFailed, MarkPendingFailed, DuplicateWorkItem, and WorkflowCompleted.
The workflow remains Express and keeps synchronous Pipe invocation.
The old duplicated persistence and branch-specific failure states are removed from the CDK definition.

tasks.title: Preserve one canonical workflow context from bootstrap through final closure
outputs: A workflow input/output contract where workItem and workflow remain available across every state and consumer results or failure metadata are attached under dedicated nodes
exit_criteria: BootstrapWorkflowInput remains the only state that understands the Pipe batch root shape.
InvokeConsumerLambda stores success output under $.consumerResult and failure output under $.workflowError.
Success and failure closure states do not replace the root workflow object.

tasks.title: Implement the claim and duplicate/no-claimable semantics exactly once
outputs: A deterministic claim path that creates idempotency first, claims pending second, rolls back idempotency if pending cannot be claimed, and terminates duplicates safely
exit_criteria: AcquireIdempotencyLock writes one IN_PROGRESS idempotency row with a conditional put.
MarkPendingInProgress conditionally changes PENDING to IN_PROGRESS.
RollbackIdempotencyLock deletes the just-created idempotency row when pending cannot be claimed.
DuplicateWorkItem terminates without invoking the consumer.

tasks.title: Normalize persistence payloads before any DynamoDB result write
outputs: PrepareSuccessPersistence and PrepareFailurePersistence states that materialize one persistence sub-object with typed string numerics and responseBodyText
exit_criteria: PrepareSuccessPersistence creates persistence.resultPk, persistence.resultSk, persistence.statusCodeText, persistence.durationMsText, persistence.responseBodyText, persistence.processedAt, and persistence.ttlText.
PrepareFailurePersistence creates the same persistence fields plus serialized failure responseBodyText.
No DynamoDB result write reads raw numeric nodes directly from $.consumerResult or $.normalizedFailure.

tasks.title: Unify results-table writes across success and failure branches
outputs: Result-table writes that use one uniform contract and no mixed DynamoDB attribute types for the same logical field
exit_criteria: PersistSuccessResult writes statusCode, durationMs, and ttl via numberFromString from persistence.*Text fields.
PersistFailureResult writes statusCode, durationMs, and ttl via numberFromString from persistence.*Text fields.
responseBody is always stored as a string in tapi-results for both success and failure rows.
Failure writes no longer use DynamoDB Map for responseBody.

tasks.title: Close success and failure lifecycle states symmetrically and safely
outputs: A closure model where success ends in COMPLETED, failure ends in FAILED, and unexpected closure-task failures are routed deliberately instead of silently leaving IN_PROGRESS state
exit_criteria: Success path updates idempotency to COMPLETED and pending to COMPLETED after PersistSuccessResult.
Terminal, transient exhausted, timeout, and unexpected paths all converge on PersistFailureResult -> MarkIdempotencyFailed -> MarkPendingFailed.
The implementation adds catch coverage on persistence/closure tasks where needed to avoid a hard workflow stop immediately after a claimed work item.

tasks.title: Update CDK workflow topology tests to the rebuilt machine
outputs: CDK tests that assert the new state names, shared failure persistence topology, and typed persistence strategy
exit_criteria: tapi-stack.state-machine.test.ts asserts the new normalized failure and persistence preparation states.
Tests no longer assert obsolete duplicated failure branches from the old machine.
Tests verify the workflow still preserves input context and uses full jitter retry.

tasks.title: Prepare manual validation inputs and workflow-debug paths for AWS
outputs: One repeatable manual validation path using real pending records and direct Start execution / start-sync-execution payloads
exit_criteria: There is one known-good success payload built from a real pending record.
There is one known-good terminal failure payload and one transient exhaustion payload built from real pending records.
The manual validation notes reflect that one state machine execution processes one record only.

tasks.title: Run local build and targeted tests for the rebuilt workflow
outputs: A locally verified state machine rebuild with passing targeted tests
exit_criteria: npm run build passes.
Targeted workflow, consumer, and bootstrap Jest suites pass.
CDK synthesis for the stack succeeds with the rebuilt machine.

tasks.title: Validate the rebuilt workflow directly in AWS against DynamoDB-backed work items
outputs: Operational proof that the rebuilt machine closes success, terminal, transient exhausted, and duplicate/no-claimable paths correctly without type failures
exit_criteria: A real HTTP 200 work item reaches PersistSuccessResult and leaves pending/idempotency in COMPLETED.
A real HTTP 400 work item reaches PersistFailureResult and leaves pending/idempotency in FAILED without retry.
A real HTTP 503 work item retries and then reaches PersistFailureResult with TRANSIENT_EXHAUSTED if attempts are consumed.
A duplicate or non-PENDING work item reaches DuplicateWorkItem without invoking the consumer.
No execution fails because DynamoDB numeric fields receive the wrong runtime type.
